item.title: Third-country national Budget measures draw fierce criticism; Aditus questions legality
item.description: Reaction to Budget 2027s tougher treatment of third-country nationals continued on Tuesday, with NGO aditus foundation calling the measures a shocking testament to the institutionalised racism in Maltas treatment of non-nationals and saying it may challenge them in court. Repubblika condemned the removal of free public transport and childcare as unjust, discriminatory and morally unacceptable, while business owner Alen Osman, who founded the Mammas Sugar chain, said foreign workers were being treated as a source of revenue. Restaurants Yiamas Greek Tavern and POSH Turkish also rallied publicly behind their staff, saying workers deserve dignity and fairness.

Sources: Times of Malta, Malta Independent, Malta Independent (Repubblika), Newsbook, Malta Today, Lovin Malta

item.title: Keith Schembris appeal over asset freezing rejected by Constitutional Court
item.description: The Constitutional Court rejected an appeal by former Office of the Prime Minister chief of staff Keith Schembri, his father Alfio Schembri, Malcolm Scerri and Robert Zammit against the freezing of their assets in a money laundering case. Presided over by Chief Justice Mark Chetcuti with Judges Anthony Ellul and Robert G. Mangion, the court held that the freezing order satisfied the proportionality requirement in light of the gravity of the charges. The four are pleading not guilty to a series of financial crimes linked to the sale of printing machinery to Progress Press Ltd.

item.title: Former orchestra CEO Sigmund Mifsud jailed six months for obstructing justice
item.description: Former Malta Philharmonic Orchestra CEO Sigmund Mifsud was sentenced to six months in prison after the court found him guilty of attempting to obstruct justice by trying to stop his former personal assistant from reporting sexual harassment allegations about another MPO employee to the police. The harassment allegations were made in 2022, and an employee testified to repeated unwanted physical contact and explicit photographs sent via WhatsApp. Mifsud was acquitted of two other charges involving violence and instilling fear of violence, and the decision is subject to appeal.

item.title: Lassane Cisse murder trial enters eighth day with investigators accusing Scicluna of cover-up
item.description: The jury trial of former soldier Lorin Scicluna continued on Tuesday as jurors were shown police footage of the accused retracing a route linked to the night Lassane Cisse was killed, and investigators challenged his account of lending his car to a stranger. Scicluna, 29, denies nine charges including murdering Cisse, a 42-year-old father of two from Ivory Coast, on 6 April 2019, with the prosecution alleging the killing was racially motivated. Police traced a white Toyota Starlet through CCTV footage showing mismatched headlight brightness and missing number plates, and told the court they found black tape and stickers allegedly used to alter the vehicle.

item.title: Yorgen Fenech granted 10 extra days to answer Attorney Generals appeal
item.description: The Court of Criminal Appeal granted Yorgen Fenechs defence an extra 10 days beyond the original 30-day period to file written submissions in response to the Attorney Generals appeal of his acquittal over the murder of journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia. Fenech was acquitted of complicity in the 2017 Bidnija car bomb killing by an eight-to-one jury verdict. His lawyers cited tight deadlines and the fact that team members had been abroad, and the request was upheld by Chief Justice Mark Chetcuti, Judge Josette Demicoli and Judge Doreen Clark.

item.title: Falzon defends Budget measures on third-country workers
item.description: Social Policy Minister Michael Falzon defended the Budget 2027 measures that will affect third-country nationals, saying they already contribute to the countrys expenses just as Maltese residents do. Speaking at a press conference, he said the government had calculated how many foreign workers will be caught by the measures and insisted the changes would not create difficulties for sectors that depend on them, such as health and social care services.

item.title: Abela rules out Maltese paying the 10 nightly eco-contribution
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela said the Maltese will not be the ones paying the new 10-a-night eco-contribution for short-let guests and 8 for hotel guests, as he defended the tourist tax rises announced in Budget 2027. Asked whether the higher charges would deter domestic tourism to Gozo, Abela said the measure was a principled choice designed to generate revenue, and noted tourist numbers have not fallen despite previous environmental tax increases. He said other Mediterranean destinations apply similar environmental tax levels.

item.title: Momentum and Moviment Graffitti criticise Budget 2027
item.description: Opposition party Momentum said Budget 2027 offers superficial fixes but misses structural change, calculating that a third-country national on minimum wage could face 772 in new annual costs from the loss of free transport, a 400 infrastructure fee and higher permit charges. Moviment Graffitti activist Andr Callus accused Finance Minister Clyde Caruana of building an economic model that relied on foreign workers and then squeezing every last drop of blood out of them. Momentum proposed the infrastructure fee instead apply to larger businesses where foreign workers make up a significant share of the workforce.

item.title: HSBC Malta Q3: adjusted profit before tax of 80m, dividend maintained
item.description: HSBC Bank Malta reported adjusted profit before tax of 80 million for the first nine months of 2026 and maintained a gross dividend of 4.6c per share, taking the year-to-date figure to 12.5c. Chief Executive Geoffrey Fichte said customer deposits grew, wealth management balances rose 8% on the same period last year, and insurance and wealth sales grew at double digits. The bank is preparing for a new majority shareholder, CrediaBank, subject to regulatory approval.

item.title: Cruise passenger traffic down 7% in third quarter, NSO reports
item.description: Total cruise passenger traffic in the third quarter of 2026 fell 7% year on year to 325,681, the National Statistics Office said, with 139 liner calls, one fewer than a year earlier. Transit passengers made up 82.3% of traffic, averaging 2,343 passengers per vessel, and EU Member States accounted for 56.2%. Italy was the largest source market at 18.3% followed by Spain at 12.7%, while British and American travellers together supplied 31.4%.

item.title: Student stipends to increase, Education Minister says
item.description: Students will receive another increase in stipends despite the measure not being mentioned in Mondays Budget speech, Education Minister Byron Camilleri said. A ministry spokesperson confirmed the boost but gave no figures, and said further announcements on budget measures not covered in the Finance Ministers speech will be made over the coming weeks. Camilleri described Budget 2027 as the largest investment in education, and said how the funds are assigned will be unveiled in coming days.

item.title: Planning Authority to introduce digital system for 3D project submissions
item.description: The Planning Authority is preparing to introduce a digital system allowing 3D models of future development projects to be submitted online, with the first phase due to start in the first quarter of 2027. The announcement was made at the authoritys annual planning conference, The Future by Design, held with policymakers, architects and other stakeholders. Chief Executive Johann Buttigieg said the wider work aims to make planning more digital and integrated, with greater use of data and geospatial information to improve decision-making.

item.title: Journalists institute disappointed over pre-Budget briefing exclusions
item.description: The Institute of Maltese Journalists said it was disappointed that some media houses were excluded from one-on-one Budget briefings held hours before the Budget 2027 speech, organised by the Office of the Prime Minister. Among those left out was the Nationalist Partys media, with IM questioning why the government deviated from the standard pre-Budget procedure of a single confidential meeting for all outlets. The journalists trade union called it a strange departure from the usual protocol without any seemingly good reason.

item.title: Maltese Erasmus+ students could have travel costs fully reimbursed under EU proposals
item.description: Maltese Erasmus+ students could have their travel costs fully reimbursed under proposed changes to the EU programme, Malta Today reported. The proposals would provide additional financial support for students from islands and remove travel cost caps that currently leave Maltese participants at a disadvantage. Erasmus+ is the EU scheme for student and staff mobility, and the changes remain at proposal stage rather than being finalised legislation.

item.title: George Degorgio cleared of threatening former partner in prison call
item.description: George Degorgio was found not guilty of threatening his former partner in a prison phone call, with the court finding insufficient evidence that his words amounted to a criminal threat. The case stemmed from a 7 December 2022 conversation in which he told her he was going to sort her out, and which she interpreted as a threat of violence. Degorgio admitted the remark but said he meant he would stop providing financial support, and he had been voluntarily paying 5,000 a month towards food and living expenses.

item.title: Xjenza Malta thematic programmes target national research priorities
item.description: Xjenza Malta said it is strengthening Maltas research and innovation scenario through a portfolio of thematic programmes designed to channel funding into areas of strategic national interest. Unlike general funding calls, the programmes are designed top-down and developed with public entities, authorities and agencies holding specialist sector expertise. They are funded through national funds administered by Xjenza Malta, with the aim of building a more cohesive research and innovation ecosystem.

item.title: Large promotional Budget 27 stickers land outside Parliament
item.description: Commuters in Valletta found giant stickers promoting the governments 2027 Budget plastered across the paving outside Parliament on Tuesday morning, hours after Finance Minister Clyde Caruanas speech. The brightly coloured stickers pose questions such as Need treatment outside of Malta? and Live on a pension?, alongside QR codes linking to information on individual measures. Caruana announced the Budget on Monday night, including a super bonus for workers, income tax cuts for parents and free therapy for children.
